claim: One of the firefly flash recordings had been accidentally mislabeled.
source: After the acceptance of the paper, we discovered that one of the firefly flash recordings had been accidentally mislabeled.
evidence: The authors directly state this discovery in the manuscript text.

claim: The problematic dataset involved an experiment with 20 fireflies.
source: The problematic dataset in question involved an experiment with 20 fireflies.
evidence: The authors explicitly identify the problematic dataset characteristics.

claim: On the evening of June 7, 2020, members of the Peleg lab conducted two separate tent experiments simultaneously.
source: On the evening of June 7, 2020, members of the Peleg lab conducted two separate tent experiments simultaneously, one of which involved a set of LEDs.
evidence: The authors describe the experimental setup from their field notes.

claim: One of the June 7, 2020 experiments involved a set of LEDs that was not part of the experiment reported in the paper.
source: On the evening of June 7, 2020, members of the Peleg lab conducted two separate tent experiments simultaneously, one of which involved a set of LEDs. This setup was not part of the experiment reported in the paper.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this setup was not part of the reported experiment.

claim: The LEDs were programmed to mimic the interburst intervals (Tb) observed in wild fireflies.
source: The LEDs were programmed to mimic the interburst intervals (Tb) observed in wild fireflies, incrementally adjusting the Tb parameter value to determine an optimal value for entrainment.
evidence: The authors describe the LED programming methodology.

claim: The distributions of 5, 10, and 15 fireflies remain unchanged between the original and corrected datasets.
source: Please note that the distributions of 5, 10, and 15ff remain unchanged.
evidence: The authors explicitly state this in the caption of Figure 1, which shows the comparison.

claim: The bin size for the interburst interval distributions is set to 3 seconds.
source: The bin size is set to 3 seconds.
evidence: The authors specify the bin size used in the analysis.

claim: The comparison between theory and experimental data is still robust after removing the problematic data recordings.
source: As expected, the comparison between theory and experimental data is still robust (Figure 2).
evidence: The authors state this conclusion and reference Figure 2 as supporting evidence.

claim: Figure 7 erroneously displayed the difference in medians between distributions instead of the intended two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov (K-S) test statistic.
source: We discovered that Figure 7 erroneously displayed the difference in medians between distributions instead of the intended two-sided Kolmogorov–Smirnov (K-S) test statistic.
evidence: The authors explicitly identify this error in the original figure.

claim: Thirty simulation trials were conducted in all cases, not ten as originally stated.
source: During our review, we also found a minor error in the Methods section, Agent-based simulation, Simulation parameters and in the original caption of Figure 7, which stated that ten simulation trials were conducted. In fact, thirty trials were run in all cases, both in the published and updated figures.
evidence: The authors explicitly correct the number of simulation trials.

claim: 10 individual fireflies were observed alone in the tent over durations between 5 min and 85 min.
source: We observed 10 individual fireflies alone in the tent, over durations between 5 min and 85 min.
evidence: The authors state the corrected experimental parameters.

claim: Individual fireflies produced flash trains at a frequency of about 2 Hz.
source: We observed that although these fireflies produced flash trains at a frequency of about 2 Hz, the delay between successive trains was apparently randomly distributed, from a few seconds to tens of minutes.
evidence: The authors report observed flash train frequency.

claim: The delay between successive flash trains in individual fireflies was apparently randomly distributed, from a few seconds to tens of minutes.
source: We observed that although these fireflies produced flash trains at a frequency of about 2 Hz, the delay between successive trains was apparently randomly distributed, from a few seconds to tens of minutes.
evidence: The authors report observed interburst interval characteristics.

claim: Three sets of experiments were carried out with 5, 10, 15, and 20 fireflies.
source: Then, we carried out three sets of experiments with 5, 10, 15, and 20 fireflies, using the segments between 9 minutes and 15 minutes.
evidence: The authors describe the experimental design.

claim: Collective burst flashing only appears at about 15 fireflies.
source: As previously reported, collective burst flashing only appears at about 15 fireflies.
evidence: The authors cite previously reported findings and confirm them in their data.

claim: The corrected beta values for N=5, 10, 15, 20 are β=0.16, 0.16, 0.20 and 0.30 respectively.
source: As shown in Fig. 3, the chosen values for beta, the additional fitting parameter introduced in the agent-based simulation, are: β=0.16, 0.16, 0.20 and 0.30 respectively for N=5, 10, 15, 20.
evidence: The authors provide the corrected parameter values with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The original beta values for N=5, 10, 15, 20 were β=0.18, 0.13, 0.12 and 0.64 respectively.
source: Original text: As shown in Fig. 3, the chosen values for beta, the additional fitting parameter introduced in the agent-based simulation, are: β=0.18, 0.13, 0.12 and 0.64 respectively for N=5, 10, 15, 20.
evidence: The authors provide the original parameter values for comparison.

claim: Both the original and corrected datasets are publicly available.
source: Both the original and corrected datasets are publicly available.
evidence: The authors state the availability of both datasets.

claim: All analyses were repeated after the data correction and confirmed that the findings are unaffected.
source: We repeated all analyses and confirmed that the findings are unaffected.
evidence: The authors state they performed validation analyses.

claim: The removal of problematic data has no effect on the main conclusions.
source: The removal has no effect on the main conclusions.
evidence: The authors state this conclusion in the caption of Figure 2.

claim: Only panel D of Figure 1 was updated in the correction.
source: The corrected Figure 1 is shown here (only panel D was updated):
evidence: The authors specify which panel was modified.

claim: The theoretical distributions were regenerated based on the revised single-firefly interburst intervals.
source: Next, based on the revised single-firefly interburst intervals, we regenerated the input envelope used in the analytical theory.
evidence: The authors describe the process of updating the theoretical model.
